case_title: Raju Ambadas Gangekar v. State of Maharashtra
accused_victim_relationship: Not stated (only a quarrel at the hotel on the night of the incident is described; no prior connection stated)
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302, s.325 (both read with s.34) as charged; Bombay Police Act s.37, s.135 as charged; conviction under IPC s.304 Part II
evidence_type: Eyewitness (beat constable PW-13); dying declaration; recovery of blood-stained clothes and gupti; chemical analysis of blood group; medical evidence
mitigating_circumstances: Incident preceded by a quarrel (High Court's basis for applying s.304 Part II rather than s.302)
trial_court_outcome: Acquitted the appellant (and three co-accused) by judgment dated 10 July 1989
high_court_outcome: Acquittal of three co-accused confirmed; appellant's acquittal reversed and convicted under IPC s.304 Part II, 5 years rigorous imprisonment and fine of INR 2,000
offence_finally_established: Culpable homicide not amounting to murder (IPC s.304 Part II)
neutral_facts: On the night of 10 July 1988, the victim, an army officer, and a colleague visited a hotel on the main road in Ahmednagar. The prosecution alleged that a quarrel broke out at the hotel between the accused and the two visitors, and that chilli powder was thrown into the eyes of the visitors, after which they ran out. The victim was allegedly chased by the accused and assaulted with a gupti, a knife-type weapon, and fell on the road. A beat constable on patrol nearby stated that he saw the accused chase and assault the victim, and that the accused was wearing a black sando banian and a lungi. The constable took the victim by rickshaw to the police station and then to the civil hospital. At the hospital, a Special Executive Magistrate recorded a dying declaration from the victim around midnight, in which the victim described the assailant's clothing. An offence was registered on that basis. The accused was arrested in the early hours of the following day, and blood-stained clothing, a vest and a lungi, was seized from him, along with a gupti recovered on his information. Chemical analysis found the blood group on the clothing matched the victim's blood group. The victim died on 23 July 1988 and the investigation was extended to a homicide offence. The prosecution examined 14 witnesses. Two independent witnesses and the panch witnesses to the seizure did not support the prosecution. The medical evidence was said to be consistent with the eyewitness account.
physical_harm: Stab injury to the left side of the body (stomach); victim died on 23 July 1988
number_of_offences: 4 charged (IPC s.302, IPC s.325, Bombay Police Act s.37, s.135; s.34 read with IPC sections); 1 finally upheld (IPC s.304 Part II)
premeditation_planning: Not identified; the court noted only that the incident was preceded by a quarrel
motive: alleged: quarrel at the hotel between the accused and the two visitors
key_evidence_accepted: Dying declaration (Exh. 21); eyewitness evidence of beat constable PW-13 on the clothing worn by the assailant; blood-stained vest and lungi recovered on arrest with blood group matching the victim; medical evidence consistent with ocular evidence
witness_credibility: PW-13 found credible and his presence at the spot natural; hostile witnesses PW-3, PW-9 and panch witnesses did not discredit the prosecution case
post_offence_conduct: Ran away from the scene after the assault (per PW-13); arrested within a few hours of the incident
bail_history: Released on bail during pendency of Supreme Court proceedings; bail bonds cancelled and appellant directed to surrender
trial_duration: offence: 10 July 1988; trial judgment: 10 July 1989; High Court: 18 March 2006; Supreme Court: 24 January 2019
legal_representation: Appellant: Sushil Karanjkar, K. N. Rai. State (respondent): Nishant Ramakantrao Katneshwarkar, Anoop Kandari
investigation_status: FIR registered under ss.326 and 307 r/w s.34 on dying declaration; investigation extended to s.302 after death; accused arrested; 14 witnesses examined; trial completed
procedural_irregularity: None noted as a fatal lapse; the defence argued absence of identification parade and non-examination of Lt. Desouza and beat constable Ram Deshmukh, which the Court did not treat as fatal
appeal_history: Trial court (10 July 1989): acquitted all four accused. High Court (18 March 2006): acquittal of three confirmed; appellant convicted under s.304 Part II, 5 years RI and fine INR 2,000. Supreme Court: appeal dismissed
prosecution_argument: Trial court's appreciation of evidence was perverse and High Court justifiably reversed acquittal; relied on beat constable PW-13's evidence, the dying declaration (Ex. 21) and the investigating officer PW-14's evidence; victim was an army man
defence_argument: Reversal of acquittal unjustified under Mookiah; trial court gave valid reasons citing investigation discrepancies; PW-13 did not see assailant's face; no identification parade; PW-3, PW-9 and panch witnesses turned hostile; blood-stained clothing recovery alone insufficient
legal_principle_applied: Appellate court may reverse acquittal where it is perverse and causes miscarriage of justice; appellate court may reappreciate evidence; interference only where two reasonable conclusions are not possible
precedent_relied_upon: K Gopal Reddy v. State of Andhra Pradesh (1979) 1 SCC 365 (relied on); Chandrappa v. State of Karnataka (2007) 4 SCC 415 (relied on); Mookiah (2013) 2 SCC 89, Murugesan (2012) 10 SCC 383 and Prem Singh (2013) 14 SCC 88 (referred to)
sentencing_rationale: Not applicable (the sentence of five years under s.304 Part II was upheld; the only reasoning stated is that the incident was preceded by a quarrel)
other_sentence_order: Bail bonds cancelled; appellant to surrender forthwith to undergo sentence; copy of judgment to Chief Judicial Magistrate for compliance
